Article Title: 'We call it kidnapping': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka calls Assam Police action completely illegal
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka . (PTI Photo)

CJP to begin nationwide protest from Oct 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam Police action was "completely illegal."Ranka, who was later released, alleged that CJP members were picked up from private property without being informed of the grounds for their detention.Ranka alleged that the police failed to provide a specific reason for the action. “It wasn't a detention. It was completely illegal because they picked us up from private property. We don't call this detention; we call it kidnapping,” he said.“When we asked the police on what grounds we were detained, their only reply was, 'Sir, we have orders from above, so we arrested you, detained you.' And even after that, when we continuously asked while we were there, they couldn't give us any other reason,” Ranka alleged.He also accused Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of attempting to suppress the organisation's activities.“The government's intention was to bully us. Hemanta Biswa Sarma wanted to intimidate us, but Hemanta Biswa Sarma made the same mistake that Amit Shah made on July 20th. The more you suppress, the more the revolution will spread,” he said.“Now, Assam CJP will see how students and youth issues will be raised in the coming times,” Ranka added.Ranka said CJP plans to expand its activities across Assam and other Northeastern states, focusing on issues concerning students and young people.“There are many issues in Assam; there are a lot of local issues here. The condition of schools here is very poor, especially in the remote areas where most schools don't even have their own buildings,” he said.“A complete facade has been created in the name of development, but we want the country to see the reality of that development,” Ranka added. He said the organisation would also raise issues related to floods, Kaziranga and other local concerns.“All the student and youth-centric issues that the youth of Assam have been struggling with for a long time, we will work on all of them in the coming time. We will definitely go to other Northeast states. We have received a very good response, a very good support,” Ranka said.The CJP leaders were detained on Sunday shortly before the organisation's first regional volunteers' meeting in Guwahati was scheduled to begin near the Assam Secretariat.The organisation said several senior leaders and Assam-based volunteers, including Ranka, Ankit Bhardwaj and Prem Aakash, were taken to a police facility. Reports said around 30 CJP workers were detained.The CJP had described the gathering as a peaceful meeting on private property. Assam Police has not publicly provided a detailed explanation for the detentions, according to the information available.Ranka also said that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had initially planned to travel to Assam following the detentions but would now focus on preparations for the organisation's proposed October 2 protest over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Abhijit's plan was based on our arrest yesterday. But as I've been released, Abhijit is not coming. He is busy preparing for the protest planned for October 2nd regarding SIR and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation,” Ranka told reporters.On the demand for Kumar's resignation, Ranka said the organisation would launch a nationwide protest from October 2.“It will happen now. For 48 hours, the ball was in Gyanesh Kumar's court. Now the ball is in CJP's court. We'll start our nationwide protest from 2nd October, and we won't back down until Ganeshkumar resigns,” he added.Ranka also alleged that more than 13 crore people had been removed from electoral rolls and questioned the process of electoral boundary redrawing in Assam. These claims were made by Ranka and CJP and have not been independently established.The remarks come amid a wider political dispute over the functioning of the Election Commission and the SIR exercise. An Indian Express report cited by CJP said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on multiple occasions over SIR-related decisions.The Election Commission has rejected allegations of internal disagreement and maintained that decisions concerning SIR were taken with the “unanimous approval of the Commission.” The detentions came after the leadership of Akhil Gogoi-led Raijor Dal met CJP leaders, including Ranka, in Guwahati.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam Police action was "completely illegal" CJP plans to expand its activities across Assam and other Northeastern states, focusing on issues concerning students and young people.

Article Title: 'No basic public safety, expressing solidarity no solution': SC pulls up system amid rising rape cases in Delhi
Article Text:
Supreme Court flags systemic gaps in Delhi’s public safety measures amid rising rape cases

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape cases in Delhi-NCR, saying the incidents point to a “systematic failure” by law-enforcement and public administrative authorities to ensure basic public safety.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the court registry to register a suo motu public interest litigation on the issue and list it for hearing."The reports of rape cases in Delhi-NCR starkly underline a systematic failure on the part of the law enforcement and the public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety," news agency PTI quoted the bench saying.The court said the incidents brought back “painful parallels” with the 2012 Nirbhaya case and raised questions over whether law-enforcement mechanisms had made meaningful progress since then."One cannot help but draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case, raising the question of whether systemic law-enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress in the decade since then," Bar and Bench quoted Justice Pardiwala saying.The bench said the right to live with dignity and without fear of violence is an intrinsic part of the fundamental right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.It said public spaces such as parks, roads, buses, metro stations, subways and footbridges cannot be allowed to become high-risk zones because of inadequate lighting, poor surveillance, lack of patrolling or other preventable administrative deficiencies.The court's observations came against the backdrop of multiple sexual assault cases reported in the national capital.A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by the conductor and driver of a sleeper bus after boarding it in Greater Noida on August 4. She was later abandoned near Kashmere Gate in Old Delhi, over 40 km away. Both accused have been arrested.The Supreme Court also said statements by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over such incidents, while understandable, do not address the larger question of institutional accountability.“Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil,” the bench said, calling for a measurable response and accountability from authorities responsible for preventing crime, maintaining public order and protecting vulnerable people.The court's intervention also follows the August 4 gang-rape of a 16-year-old girl on a sleeper bus in Greater Noida. The teenager was allegedly assaulted by the bus conductor and driver and abandoned near Kashmere Gate, over 40 km away. Both accused have been arrested.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the court registry to register a suo motu public interest litigation on the issue. The court said the incidents brought back “painful parallels” with the 2012 Nirbhaya case and raised questions over whether law-enforcement mechanisms had made meaningful progress.

Article Title: CBSE third-language rule: Supreme Court extends relaxations to Class VI students
Article Text:
SC extends Class VII-VIII relaxations to Class VI (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the CBSE to extend to Class VI students the same exemptions and relaxations available to students of Classes VII and VIII under its newly introduced three-language scheme.Under the order, Class VI students will have to study the newly mandated third language, but they will not have to appear for a CBSE Board examination in that language when they reach Class X. The exemption is currently available to students who are in Classes VII and VIII.The Supreme Court has also extended another relaxation to Class VI students. Those already studying two non-native languages will be allowed to continue with the same combination and take one additional Bharatiya Bhasha as their third language.This means such students will not have to drop or change either of their existing languages to accommodate the two regional languages required under the new language scheme.The directions bring Class VI students on par with the current Classes VII and VIII batches in terms of the exemptions and flexibility available under the CBSE's three-language policy.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders CBSE to extend same exemptions and relaxations to Class VI students. Students will have to study the newly mandated third language, but will not have to appear for a CBSE Board examination in that language. The exemption is currently available to students who are in Classes VII and VIII.

Article Title: J&K assembly passes resolution seeking urgent restoration of full statehood amid BJP walkout
Article Text:
J&K assembly passes Omar’s statehood resolution amid BJP walkout

NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir legislative assembly on Monday passed a resolution demanding the urgent restoration of full statehood to the Union Territory, amid strong protests and walkout from BJP legislators.The resolution was moved by chief minister Omar Abdullah and was passed despite opposition from the BJP, the largest opposition party in the assembly.Jammu and Kashmir has remained a Union Territory since the BJP-led Centre abrogated Article 370 in August 2019 and reorganised the erstwhile state into two Union Territories, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.The BJP opposed the resolution, questioning the manner in which it was allowed by Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather. BJP legislators said the Speaker had permitted the resolution to be taken up in relaxation of the assembly rules.As soon as the assembly proceedings began on Monday, BJP members stood up and protested against the resolution.The opposition party also moved a motion seeking the removal of Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather, alleging that he had allowed the chief minister's resolution in violation of the rules.
Article Summary: The resolution was moved by chief minister Omar Abdullah and was passed despite opposition from the BJP, the largest opposition party in the assembly. Jammu and Kashmir has remained a Union Territory since the BJP-led Centre abrogated Article 370 in August 2019 and reorganised the erstwhile state into two Union Territories.

Article Title: SC asks EC to decide TMC name, symbol dispute between rival factions within 3 months
Article Text:
SC directs EC to settle TMC faction dispute over name, ‘flowers and grass’ symbol

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Election Commission to decide the dispute between two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress (TMC) over the party's name and its “flowers and grass” election symbol within three months.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked both factions to complete their pleadings before the poll panel within four weeks.The court directed the Election Commission to take a final decision on the dispute within three months after the completion of pleadings by both sides.The court passed the order while hearing a plea filed by former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee challenging the EC’s decision to freeze the TMC’s name and “flowers and grass” election symbol.The development comes days after the Election Commission temporarily allotted Mamata Banerjee’s faction the name “Mamata All India Trinamool Congress” and the “football player” symbol. The rival faction was allotted the name “Democratic Trinamool Congress” and the “envelope” symbol.Earlier, in an interim order, the poll panel froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and its “flowers and grass” symbol after recognising a factional dispute within the party.Neither faction can use the original name or symbol until the dispute is finally settled.The temporary arrangement will apply to the upcoming bypolls, with candidates from the two factions contesting under the separate names and symbols allotted by the Commission.The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both factions have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the poll panel after rival groups staked claims to control the TMC. The Commission subsequently sought submissions on issues including organisational control, authorised office-bearers, party assets, the party name and its election symbol.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has been hearing competing claims over control of the party, its name and election symbol. The dispute reached the poll panel after rival groups staked claims to control the TMC. Neither faction can use the original name or symbol until the dispute is finally settled.

Article Title: ‘Will contest at least 150 seats in UP’: Congress discusses alliance talks with SP
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: The Congress will contest at least 150 seats in the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections early next year, a party leader said on Monday, asserting that the Congress is “entitled” to contest half the seats in its alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP).Seat-sharing talks with the SP are likely to be finalised in October, according to Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ Uttar Pradesh in-charge.“Seat-sharing will likely be finalised in October. Congress has candidates available to contest all 403 seats. Under the alliance, the Congress is entitled to 50% of the seats. We will not contest fewer than 150 seats,” Gautam told ANI.“For the last two months, Congress has been working on seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh. Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi, KC Venugopal and I are looking after this work,” he added.The Congress and the SP are key constituents of the Opposition INDIA bloc in Uttar Pradesh. The two parties contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state as alliance partners, winning 43 of the 80 seats. The SP won 37 seats — its best performance in a Lok Sabha election — while the Congress secured six. The BJP, which rules both the Centre and the state, finished second with 33 seats, down from 62 in 2019.The previous SP-Congress alliance in Uttar Pradesh, for the 2017 assembly elections, was less successful. The SP won 47 seats and was voted out of power, while the Congress secured only seven seats.
Article Summary: Seat-sharing talks with the SP are likely to be finalised in October, according to Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ Uttar Pradesh in-charge. The previous SP- Congress alliance in Uttar Pradesh, for the 2017 assembly elections, was less successful. The SP won 47 seats and was voted out of power.

Article Title: Bank unions call off 3-day strike after assurances, IBA to study demands
Article Text:
Bank unions withdraw three-day strike after late-night agreement with IBA on key demands.

NEW DELHI: Bank unions called off their proposed three-day strike just before midnight after the Indian Banks Association agreed to look into their demands."A high-level committee of IBA and UFBU (United Forum of Bank Unions) will be formed immediately to deliberate on the issue of declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays. This committee will explore, all possible alternatives; discuss with all stakeholders, and work out a solution acceptable to all stakeholders and, more importantly, the customers," a late night communication said.Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers.The late-night announcement came after what turned out to be a working Sunday for state-run bank employees as govt ordered branches to stay open so that customers are not inconvenienced.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex crashes over 1,100 points, investors lose Rs 8.92 lakh crore - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.

Why is stock market crashing today?

Iran-US conflict escalates

Oil prices jump

Bond yields soar

Rupee tumbles

FII outflows

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks tanked in morning trade on Monday as persistently high crude oil prices and a spike in US bond yields added to investors’ woes. Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.While Sensex crashed over 1,100 points, Nifty50 went below 22,800. At 3:29 PM, Nifty50 was trading at 22,788.25, down 352 points or 1.52%. BSE Sensex was at 72,805.78, down 1,090 points or 1.47%.The selloff also erased nearly Rs 8.92 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to around Rs 474 lakh crore.Also Read | Two years ago Sensex hit lifetime high: What went wrong after that & what’s the road ahead? Every one of the 30 Sensex stocks was trading in negative territory. Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HDFC Bank led the decline. The weakness was not restricted to large-cap stocks. The Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices also declined by more than 1% each.Indian equities were also tracking the broader weakness across several Asian markets, where stocks came under pressure amid the surge in oil prices.South Korea’s Kospi declined more than 2%, while China’s Shanghai Composite dropped over 1.7%. Japan’s Nikkei, however, posted muted gains.Tensions between Iran and the US intensified after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire along with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Trump said, "I reject this agreement. They want an agreement to be made under which the Strait of Hormuz is immediately opened, because they are severely failing.”Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said the country would remain firm and would not back down in the face of the US and Israel.The latest developments in the Middle East triggered another sharp rise in crude prices, with oil gaining 2% and moving close to $107 per barrel as markets factored in the possibility of further disruption to shipments. JPMorgan said it could no longer clearly assess where oil prices were headed and, for the first time since the Iran war began in February, said it did not have a defined baseline scenario for the market.US bond yields continued their climb, reaching fresh multi-year highs and adding another layer of pressure on equities. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note moved further above 5.2%, its highest level since 2004. The 30-year US bond yield also crossed 5.5%, while the yield on two-year Treasury notes, which generally moves alongside expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes, rose above 4.9%.Higher bond yields generally increase the attractiveness of debt markets for investors, which can put additional pressure on riskier assets such as equities.The Indian rupee weakened by 14 paise to 95.89 against the US dollar in early trading. Forex traders are increasingly concerned about the currency breaching the psychologically important 96 level against the dollar, with the rupee facing pressure from elevated oil prices, higher US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.“Volatility in crude and gold, along with a rise in the dollar, limited the rupee’s ability to sustain gains. Going ahead, currency movement is likely to remain range-bound amid global commodity and dollar volatility. Rupee range can be seen between 95.50-96.50,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.Foreign investors continued to sell Indian equities on Friday, offloading shares worth a net Rs 3,694 crore, according to provisional NSE data.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said the shift in FPI flows towards the negative side after positive inflows in July and August had become visible earlier this month. He said the selling trend has continued, with total equity outflows through exchanges reaching Rs 25,682 crore so far this month.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict. Selloff erased nearly Rs 8.92 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies. Every one of the 30 Sensex stocks was trading in negative territory.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Balakot to Sindoor, India gave befitting reply: PM Modi on Pakistan terror
Article Text:
PM Modi’s stern message to Pakistan: ‘Time for sponsoring terror to go unpunished is long gone’

'Zero-tolerance terror policy has borne results'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to Pakistan, PM Modi said on Sunday the time when its role in sponsoring terror attacks on India would go unpunished is long gone, and his govt has made it clear with its actions, including Op Sindoor, that terrorists will be given a befitting response for their sinister designs against India.Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror. The strike demonstrated a new aspect of India's counter-terror policy. It was our decisive response to long-standing pain India had endured," he said."Over the past decade, from Balakot airstrike to Op Sindoor, India has repeatedly sent out a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response."Contrasting his government's targeted action against Pakistan to the approach of the previous Congress-led UPA govt, PM Narendra Modi said serial blasts had once become a common occurrence in the country. On Sept 13, 2008, serial blasts rocked Delhi and, just a few weeks later, the Mumbai terror attack stunned the country, the PM said.Demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack used to be made then but were ignored. "Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that," he said.During Op Sindoor, the Modi govt also unveiled a tougher national security doctrine, declaring that any future terror attack will be treated as an act of war. This eliminated the false distinction between terrorists and their state sponsors, it had said.Modi's message to Pakistan comes at a time when the nation is trying to airbrush its long association with terror incidents around the world, reflected in its PM Shehbaz Sharif's recent claims at the United Nations General Assembly about its role and sacrifices in combating terrorism.In his UNGA address, foreign minister S Jaishankar had snubbed Pakistan, calling it a "serial practitioner of terrorism" and asserting that India will continue to exercise its right to defend itself against terror threats.
Article Summary: Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror," he said.

Article Title: Why are gold prices crashing today? MCX Gold down Rs 3,200/10 grams, plunges over 2% - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Gold remains under pressure as both bond yields and crude oil prices moved higher.

Why is gold crashing today?

What’s the outlook?

How should you trade gold?

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold price crash today: The start of the week saw both the precious metals, MCX Gold and MCX Silver, crash on Monday as the rise in oil prices fuelled inflation worries and increased expectations that the US Federal Reserve could raise interest rates further.On the domestic bourse, MCX silver futures for September 2026 delivery fell Rs 6,661 to Rs 2,28,035 per kg. Gold futures for October 2026 delivery declined Rs 3,214 to Rs 1,47,667 per 10 grams.In international markets, spot gold was down 1.5% at $4,223.95 per ounce as of 0117 GMT, while US gold futures declined 1.5% to $4,257.90.Other precious metals also traded lower. Spot silver fell 2.6% to $62.64 per ounce, platinum declined 2.1% to $1,741.45 and palladium dropped 2.1% to $1,239.95.Gold remains under pressure as both bond yields and crude oil prices moved higher. The increase in oil prices, driven by mixed indications on supply flows, kept inflation risks firmly in focus among investors.Iran said diplomacy remained the only route to resolving its conflict with the United States and Israel. This came after US President Donald Trump said he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and bring the fighting to an end.Oil prices later recovered more than 1%.According to experts, the primary reason for prices falling sharply is the rise in US bond yields.Ashish Rajodiya, Head – Commodities, PL Capital says, “MCX Gold (December contract) is trading at Rs 1,50,500 per 10 grams, down Rs 2,700 or 1.80% today, extending its slide for a second straight week. The pressure is coming from a sharp US Treasury bond selloff - the 10-year yield at 5.13%, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year at 5.44%, its highest since 2004.”CME FedWatch data indicates that markets are now pricing a 68.1% probability of another 25 basis points rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in its October-end meeting. Earlier, the odds were just 31.9%.“Elevated crude prices, rather than boosting gold's safe-haven appeal as they typically would during geopolitical stress, are instead reinforcing the case for further Fed tightening, feeding a stronger dollar and steeper yield curve that both work against non-yielding bullion,” he says.Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities explains, “Global commodities are trading under pressure, with precious metals under sharp pressure as crude remains firm. Uncertainty around the US-Iran conflict continues to keep risk sentiment volatile. Recent diplomatic efforts have produced mixed signals, with Iran indicating readiness for both negotiations and renewed conflict, while the US has rejected Iran’s latest proposal, although further talks through mediators remain possible. ”“Gold is trading at $4185, down more than 2.%, and it is facing sharp selling pressure as geopolitical uncertainty, a firm Dollar and higher bond yields with 5.22% on 10yrs weigh on bullion as higher probability of rate hike prices in. The lack of clarity over a potential US-Iran settlement is keeping safe-haven demand volatile,” he adds.Ashish Rajodiya is of the view that gold prices have support at Rs 1,48,000 and Rs 1,46,000, with resistance at Rs 1,52,500 and Rs 1,55,000.“The metal's next move likely hinges on two threads converging at once: the Fed's October rate decision, and whether the recent signs of renewed US-Iran diplomatic engagement on Hormuz firm up into an actual de-escalation,” he says.“A dovish surprise from the Fed or confirmed progress on Iran talks could spark a sharp bounce toward resistance, while continued hawkish signals or a stalled Iran negotiation would likely extend the slide toward the lower support band,” he adds.Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart expects gold and silver to see continued volatility this week as traders track movements in crude oil prices and the dollar index, along with geopolitical tensions and developments in the US-Iran peace talks.For gold, he sees support at $4,284-4,260 per troy ounce, with resistance placed at $4,355-4,388. In silver, support is at $63.80-63.00 per troy ounce, while resistance stands at $65.50-66.60.On the MCX, Jain has identified support for gold at Rs 1,50,150-1,49,600 and resistance at Rs 1,51,400-1,52,000. For silver, his support levels are Rs 2,33,000-2,30,400, with resistance at Rs 2,36,600-2,38,800.Jain told ET that investors should wait for further developments in the US-Iran peace talks before initiating fresh positions in gold and silver. For those already holding long positions, he recommended keeping a strict stop-loss below Rs 1,49,600 for gold and below Rs 2,30,000 for silver, based on daily closing levels.

Article Title: Stone pelting, tear gas and clashes with police: Why Ujjain is on the boil
Article Text:
The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain.

What happened at the site

City Qazi appeals for peace

Road widening for Simhastha

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ujjain prepares for 2028 gathering

NEW DELHI: Tensions rose in Ujjain on Monday as protesters clashed with police during demonstrations over development work in the city. Police were deployed in large numbers around the Shahi Masjid Complex as sporadic protests and stone pelting were reported in the area.The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028, with authorities planning a major infrastructure overhaul ahead of the religious gathering.Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred when a large group of people clashed with them at the spot where a portion of Shahi Masjid was planned to be demolished.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel has been deployed at the spot.SP Pradeep Sharma said: "Police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd. Leaders from the Muslim community are also issuing video messages urging calm.""All communities and sections of society are continuously extending their cooperation and support in their respective areas. Even today, the demolition work, initiated by the mosque committee itself, is underway at the Shahi Masjid.As a precautionary measure, a full security perimeter has been established, and entry is prohibited for everyone. However, certain miscreants attempted to create a disturbance and resorted to stone-pelting. The police personnel present at the scene responded by using tear gas and mild force to disperse the crowd," he said.Sharma said the cops utilised tear gas to manage the situation and that "entire area is being monitored via CCTV and drones".The officer futher said: "We will now identify the perpetrators using CCTV and drone footage and register FIRs against those found involved. An attempt to block the road was also made by some women; however, after being counseled and shown video footage of the situation, they withdrew the blockade. The road is open. I appeal to everyone to please cooperate; if anyone engages in such activities, strict action will be taken against them. As you can all see, this entire undertaking is being carried out by the committee itself, with everyone's consent."Protesters tried to move through narrow lanes towards the area, with some women seen being pushed forward as the crowd attempted to proceed. Stones were also thrown at police personnel deployed to maintain order.The situation remained tense as security forces stayed at the spot to prevent further escalation.Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi, meanwhile, criticised the demolition and urged the Madhya Pradesh government to take public sentiment into account."The administrative efforts to demolish the Ujjain Shahi Masjid under the pretext of road widening should be a bit more sensitive. Demolishing a 600-year-old heritage site just for road widening and development in the name of progress is the height of hatred. It has come to my notice that when the matter is pending in court, what message does the administration intend to send by repeatedly laying siege to the masjid? Thousands of youth in Ujjain are continuously raising their voices on this issue. My request to the Ujjain administration is to respect public sentiments and acquire the necessary land for road widening from the other side. Demolishing such a historically significant heritage site cannot be considered a normal event under any circumstances," the Congress MP said.Qazi Khaliqur Rahman appealed to members of the Muslim community to maintain peace and urged them not to gather unnecessarily in markets or venture towards market areas.In a statement, the City Qazi urged people not to pay heed to rumours and remain inside their homes, maintaining that the issue concerning the mosque had already been resolved during the night.“The members of the community are informed not to stand unnecessarily in the markets or go towards the market areas. The issue related to the mosque was resolved during the night itself. There is no such matter that requires anyone to come out,” he said.The demolition is part of a larger road-widening exercise in Ujjain. Authorities have identified 272 structures for demolition as preparations intensify for the 2028 Simhastha gathering.Earlier, chief minister Mohan Yadav had participated in demolition work at his ancestral home. He said giving up the property had been emotionally difficult but was necessary for the wider development project."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.Yadav said his decision was also intended to encourage other residents affected by the project to cooperate with the administration."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation chairperson Kalawati Yadav said preparations for Simhastha include several major infrastructure projects. The event is held once every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River and is expected to draw millions of devotees."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening project is part of the wider redevelopment plan aimed at improving Ujjain's infrastructure and handling the expected influx of pilgrims during the 2028 Simhastha Mela.
Article Summary: Police used tear gas shells to control a crowd in the city as stone pelting occurred. The clashes erupted after the demolition of a portion of the Shahi Masjid as part of a road-widening project. The work is linked to preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028.

SC cancels Mhatre’s bail in doctor assault case, stays Bombay HC order

The Supreme Court has cancelled the bail granted by the Bombay High Court to Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting a doctor at a civic hospital. The court also stayed the High Court order granting him bail on a plea filed by the Maharashtra government.While cancelling Mhatre’s bail, the Supreme Court said the message should go “loud and clear” that the medical fraternity cannot be touched.A court in Maharashtra had framed charges against Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and four others over the assault of doctors, including a female doctor, and nurses at Dombivli’s Shastri Nagar Municipal Hospital following a dispute over the treatment of a pregnant woman on July 6.Mhatre, along with Pramod Nikam, Ramesh Pawar, Akshay Karande and Sadhana Karande, appeared before Fast-Track Court Judge N P Vasade two days after police filed a 1,832-page chargesheet in the case.The accused have been charged under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to assault and causing hurt, assaulting or obstructing a public servant, unlawful assembly and rioting, common intention, criminal intimidation and intentional insult, besides offences relating to the dignity or modesty of a woman.They have also been booked under Sections 3 and 4 of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act and Sections 37(1)(3) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act for allegedly violating orders imposed to maintain public order.Mhatre had been staying in Goa after the Bombay High Court granted him conditional bail in August. The High Court had directed him to remain outside Maharashtra until the chargesheet was filed and ordered that the trial be fast-tracked for completion within three months.After the chargesheet was filed, the condition ceased to operate, following which Mhatre returned to his residence and appeared before the court earlier this month.

Article Title: SIR row: Nadda backs EC, sends message to Rahul Gandhi and opposition
Article Text:
Nadda​ accused the oppn of repeatedly raising allegations despite responses from the Election Commission.

Kharge demands CEC's resignation

Rahul Gandhi's allegations over SIR

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR row surrounding the Election Commission , saying, “repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth”.Nadda also targeted Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, accusing them of attempting to “malign and weaken” the country's autonomous and constitutional institutions.Speaking to reporters, Nadda took a direct aim at the Congress leader saying, “Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated.”“For Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal, Akhilesh Yadav, and Mamata Banerjee, the sole agenda has become to malign and weaken the nation's autonomous and constitutional institutions. This is the same 'toolkit mentality' that hatches a new conspiracy every morning to stall the country's development: level allegations, disrupt the national atmosphere, and flee. This has become the opposition's modus operandi,” he said.“They care nothing for national security, public welfare, or the country's honor and prestige. Their only objective is to seize power, not to serve the people, but to nurture dynastic politics and reap personal benefits... The public has taught a befitting lesson to the forces seeking to create instability in the country in the past, and in the future too; every delusion and conspiracy of theirs will be shattered in the court of the people,” he added.Nadda further accused the opposition of continuing to raise allegations despite the Election Commission’s responses, saying it was attempting to create confusion and disrupt the atmosphere in the country.“Today, as the nation realizes the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) through the tireless efforts of its 1.4 billion citizens, and as India’s influence resonates across the global stage, the Congress and the entire 'INDI Alliance' are, unfortunately, frustrated and despondent at this progress..." Nadda said."Lacking policies and a vision, they are now devising new ploys to spread confusion and anarchy across the country. We all witnessed the uproar created nationwide just a few days ago over a fabricated story. Now, even after the Election Commission has exposed every lie they propagated, they are once again attempting to vitiate the atmosphere,” Nadda added.He alleged that Rahul and Kejriwal “make allegations and walk away; they have nothing to do with public interest.”The Union minister further accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking “intent and vision”.“We saw a few days ago how an attempt was made to disturb the atmosphere across the country on the basis of a fabricated news report. Now, even after all members of the Election Commission have responded to their allegations, they are once again engaged in efforts to vitiate the atmosphere in the country,” Nadda said.Nadda also contrasted the BJP 's approach to power with that of the opposition, saying, “For BJP, power is a means to serve the interests of 140 crore people.”He said the BJP's objective was to serve citizens and fulfil its commitment to Antyodaya, while accusing the Opposition of seeking power for dynastic politics and its own interests.Nadda's remarks came after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and other leaders demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that he was propagating the BJP's philosophy.“They will say like this only, but their own people have exposed them, and their own people are telling. Even a Chief Secretary of Kerala says, our CEC himself told him to contest the election. It means that a person who is in the highest position is propagating the BJP’s philosophy, and he has become a BJP worker. So it is clear. There is nothing. He should resign. If he has got any little moral right, he should resign from that post. And afterwards, we have to take action against him, even after resignation,” Kharge said.“I have called a working committee meeting for tomorrow, and there we'll discuss; all the working committee members will give their suggestions. And we are going to fight seriously. This issue concerns the entire country, the existence of our democracy, and the country's survival. That's why we are very serious about this issue. We'll fight, and we'll see that,” he added.The political row comes amid opposition criticism of the Election Commission's handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul Gandhi had earlier alleged that the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were “all rigged” and demanded the immediate resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.He also accused the CEC of “match-fixing elections”, citing a news channel report claiming that Kumar had approached former Kerala chief secretary Jiji Thomson to contest the 2026 Assembly elections on a BJP ticket.The Election Commission, meanwhile, clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary that had drawn scrutiny related to the functioning of an officer on deputation to the poll body and not to any policy matter.The row also follows an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and orders related to SIR and other electoral matters. The reported objections included issues concerning Form 6, voter deletions and access to electoral-roll databases.The poll body rejected the suggestion that these objections amounted to institutional dissent over final decisions, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process.The Election Commission maintained that all decisions taken by it, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of all three commissioners, PTI reported.Opposition parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT), have demanded Kumar's resignation.Meanwhile, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya said an INDIA bloc meeting is expected on September 30 to discuss the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission.
Article Summary: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday attacked the opposition and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR row. He said, “repeating a lie a hundred times does not make it the truth; the truth cannot be defeated” He accused the opposition of attempting to create confusion and disturb the atmosphere in the country despite lacking “intent and vision”

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”

Article Title: 2,000 cops deployed, classes suspended for 10 days: Lovely Professional University protests spiral into violence - top developments
Article Text:
Rape claim, campus unrest and midnight clashes: What happened at LPU

Police deploy over 2,000 personnel

Clashes, arson and highway blockade

Rape case registered, SIT formed

LPU denies rape claim, releases students' video

Congress attacks Punjab government

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most critical issue that needs to be addressed by the university? Campus safety and security Mental health support for students Transparency in handling complaints Proper investigation of the alleged incident 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night.

Article Title: CCPA penalises Amazon, Flipkart, JioMart for selling unregistered herbicide
Article Text:
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product, Cyclosinone Herbicide.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds in lawns, gardens and agricultural fields.In separate orders issued recently, the consumer watchdog directed the e-commerce marketplaces to immediately discontinue the false and misleading advertisements and conduct a self-audit of their platforms to identify and remove products that violate the law or pose a risk to consumers’ life and safety.The CCPA initiated proceedings after the department of agriculture and farmers’ welfare forwarded a complaint it had received from the Crop Care Federation of India (CCFI) regarding the sale and advertisement of the unregistered herbicide through e-commerce and digital media platforms.During the investigation, the agriculture department informed CCPA that the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides and pesticides are regulated under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and the Insecticides Rules to safeguard human beings and animals from potential risks.The department told the authority that no chemical named Cyclosinone is included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act. However, a product marketed as “Cyclosinone Herbicide” was being sold through online platforms without disclosing the chemical name of its active ingredient or its composition.“It is currently being marketed illegally because it bypasses the mandatory safety, bio-efficacy, quality and legal checks required under the Insecticides Act,” the department said in its submission to CCPA.The authority rejected the e-commerce companies’ argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers. The CCPA said online marketplaces cannot disown their statutory obligation to protect consumers and are required to exercise due diligence to prevent the sale of products that are illegal or hazardous.
Article Summary: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart. Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note

The controversy

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.

Article Title: 'Left' in existential crisis: From CPI-CPM rift in Kerala to Delhi rout, old fault lines deepen
Article Text:
The Left faces a deeper political challenge as electoral setbacks, internal tensions and shrinking influence converge

Pinarayi probe: Another challenge after Kerala defeat

DUSU polls: Why isn't Left mobilisation becoming votes?

CPI vs CPM: When opposition itself becomes a battlefield

From Bengal to Kerala: How did the Left reach here?

Poll Vote & Share your view How pivotal is the recent defeat in Kerala for the future of the Left in India? Extremely pivotal Moderately pivotal Not very pivotal Not pivotal at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion
